misconceptions.description: Treating synthesis as summarizing each module topic in turn rather than making the topics act together on one design decision.
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes separate paragraphs summarizing each topic with no shared artifact
misconceptions.feedback: Synthesis converges several principles on one concrete decision and explains how they interact. Replace parallel summaries with one integrated decision brief.

misconceptions.description: Believing that naming many module terms in a justification counts as integration, even when no principle changes the design.
misconceptions.trigger: learner inserts module terms into captions without letting any principle alter the artifact
misconceptions.feedback: A term only counts when it changes a design choice. Show how each cited principle reshaped the screen, not just that it was mentioned.

misconceptions.description: Applying competing principles at full strength on the same screen without acknowledging or resolving the tension between them.
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds support and removes redundancy on the same element without noting the conflict
misconceptions.feedback: When principles compete, name the tension, decide which governs for this learner and goal, and justify the tradeoff.
